error.signature: AI tells a foreigner moving to Greece that an EHIC card covers their ongoing healthcare, or that AMKA is optional for legal employment

verdict.summary: AMKA (Αριθμός Μητρώου Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης), an 11-digit social security registration number, has been mandatory since October 2009 for legal employment and residence-based healthcare access in Greece. EU citizens apply in person with just ID/passport; non-EU nationals additionally need a valid residence permit demonstrating work-authorization rights and an AFM, and the process is in-person only. Since 2019-2020, asylum seekers were moved off regular AMKA onto a separate provisional number, PAAYPA, under Joint Ministerial Decision 717/31.01.2020; recognized refugees are entitled to the regular permanent AMKA. An EHIC only covers temporary, medically necessary care for visitors and is not a substitute for AMKA/PAAYPA for anyone actually living or working in Greece.

dead_ends.action: Tell an EU citizen moving to Greece for work that their EHIC (European Health Insurance Card) covers their healthcare once they're a resident, so they don't need to register for AMKA
dead_ends.why_fails: EHIC only covers temporary, medically necessary treatment during a visit; it is not a substitute for the social-insurance registration (AMKA) required for legal employment and ongoing residence-based healthcare access, which has been mandatory since October 2009.
dead_ends.condition: EU citizen taking up residence or employment in Greece

dead_ends.action: Tell a non-EU/third-country national they can get an AMKA the same way an EU citizen does, or that any asylum seeker gets regular AMKA
dead_ends.why_fails: Non-EU nationals must first hold a residence permit demonstrating work-authorization rights (and typically an AFM) before applying for AMKA, in person only - there is no online submission. Since Joint Ministerial Decision 717/31.01.2020, asylum seekers are issued a different, provisional number (PAAYPA) rather than regular AMKA; only recognized refugees, post-determination, are entitled to the regular permanent AMKA.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That AMKA and PAAYPA are interchangeable, or that the pre-2019 rule (asylum seekers getting regular AMKA) is still current.

workarounds.action: EU citizens: register for AMKA in person at an e-EFKA branch or a KEP (citizen service center) with ID/passport. Non-EU citizens: obtain a residence permit and AFM first, then apply for AMKA in person at e-EFKA/KEP with those documents
workarounds.how: The AMKA process has no digital/online submission route - it requires an in-person visit with the correct documents for your citizenship category.
workarounds.condition: Foreigner establishing residence or employment in Greece

workarounds.action: Asylum seekers should apply for PAAYPA (not standard AMKA) through the Asylum Service under the current Joint Ministerial Decision framework
workarounds.condition: Pending asylum application, not yet recognized as a refugee

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers EHIC eligibility for temporary visitors; this one covers AMKA/PAAYPA, the separate registration needed for employment and ongoing residence-based healthcare access.

AFM is a tax registration number needed for banking, leases, and contracts; AMKA is a separate social-security number needed for employment and healthcare. Non-EU applicants typically need AFM before they can get AMKA.
